source_references.full_readback:
Write \(L=\log x\), \(E(x)=\psi(x)-x\), \(e(L)=E(e^L)e^{-L}\).
B0 is the cumulative original corpus, not full RH; B1 is B0 with
exactly INPUT_CONTRACT.json, namely
\[
 |\psi(x)-x|\le \frac1{64}\,x^{27/32}(\log x)^2
 \quad\text{for every real }x\ge e^{200}.
\]
Terminating decimal constants are rational.
Set
\[
 b_0=7/8,\quad b_1=27/32,\quad a_j=1-b_j,\quad
 H=3000175332800,\quad h=\log H,\quad \lambda=\frac{\pi}{H-1-\pi/3}.
\]

## 1. Why the new input works before exp(200)

OpenAIQRH Theorem 1.1 (PDF p.4, text lines 255–262) puts the nontrivial
zeta zeros in \(\Re\rho\le b_0\), with equality allowed. FiniteRH
Theorem 1 (PDF p.2, lines 48–52) puts those of positive height at most
\(H\) on the half line. Conjugation supplies negative heights.
There are no real zeros inside \(0<s<1\): the real alternating eta
series is positive there and equals \((1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)\).

In B1, for \(\Re s>1\) summation by parts of the Euler series gives
\[
 -\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)=s/(s-1)+s\int_1^\infty E(t)t^{-s-1}\,dt .
\]
The integral through \(e^{200}\) is entire; the rest is holomorphic
on \(\Re s>27/32\) by the exact input, locally uniformly also after
differentiation. Meromorphic continuation gives the identity there;
a zero would cause a pole of the logarithmic derivative. Thus the
new zero cutoff, with its boundary still allowed, applies at ALL
heights and is usable also for \(x<e^{200}\).

source_references.full_readback:
For \(L\ge40\) use FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8, text 631–642) with
\(T=e^{L/3}\). The admissible tuple is \((40,1/2,0,2.091)\);
\(T>\max(51,L)\) and \(5T+2<e^{L/2}\) at 40 and thereafter.
It gives, for some \(T^*\le2.45T\),
\[
 |e(L)|\le 2.091Le^{-L/3}
       +2\sum_{0<\gamma\le T^*} e^{-(1-\Re\rho)L}/\gamma.
\]
We do not assume that \(T^*\) is independent of \(x\). We use this
theorem, not the older Dudek truncation in FKS Proposition 3.4
whose underlying issues are noted in FKS Remark 3.3.

source_references.full_readback:
Take \(s_i=i/3200,\ i_0=2400,\ n_0=2800,\ n_1=2700\).
Let \(B_i=\min_{i_0\le r\le i}\overline B(s_r)\) where the bar is the
outward upper rational endpoint of S3 computed by bounds.py (BS).
For the jth mesh set \(B_{n_j}=0\) in the following expression
(artificial terminal coefficient, not an assertion of zero density
at \(b_j\)):
\[
 S_j(L)=\sum_{i=i_0}^{n_j-1}(B_i-B_{i+1})e^{-(1-s_{i+1})L},
 \quad D_j(L)=2.091Le^{-L/3}+(L^2/16)e^{-L/4}+S_j(L).         \tag{S4}
\]
Majorize the exponential by its value at the top of each bin,
the last bin being closed on the right. Write the increasing step
function as its first value plus its **nonnegative** successive
increments times the indicators of the upper tails. Bound each tail
by \(B_i\) and collect terms to get \(S_j\). This never subtracts
two upper bounds on actual zero counts. The low real-part zeros
use the \(L^2/16\) bound above, and the formula proves \(|e(L)|\le D_j(L)\).

BS=[]
for i in range(2400,2800):
    u=B(i).r
    BS.append(min(u,BS[-1]) if BS else u)
END=[2800,2700]
def spec(j):
    end=END[j];bs=BS[:end-2400]
    return [(1-I(i)/3200,I(u)-v) for i,u,v in zip(range(2401,end+1),bs,bs[1:]+[Q(0)]) if u!=v]
SPECT=[spec(j) for j in (0,1)]
# To evaluate across many cells, share one common power table per argument.
@lru_cache(maxsize=15000)
def ds(L):
    L=I(L); w=(-L/3200).exp()
    acc=I(0); head=I(0)
    x0=w**800
    for i in range(2400,2800):
        x0/=w
        v=(I(BS[i-2400])-BS[i-2399])*x0 if i<2799 else I(0)
        if i==2699: head=acc+BS[i-2400]*x0

Take \(s_i=i/3200,\ i_0=2400,\ n_0=2800,\ n_1=2700\).
Let \(B_i=\min_{i_0\le r\le i}\overline B(s_r)\) where the bar is the
outward upper rational endpoint of S3 computed by bounds.py (BS).
For the jth mesh set \(B_{n_j}=0\) in the following expression
(artificial terminal coefficient, not an assertion of zero density
at \(b_j\)):
\[
 S_j(L)=\sum_{i=i_0}^{n_j-1}(B_i-B_{i+1})e^{-(1-s_{i+1})L},
 \quad D_j(L)=2.091Le^{-L/3}+(L^2/16)e^{-L/4}+S_j(L).         \tag{S4}
\]
Majorize the exponential by its value at the top of each bin,
the last bin being closed on the right. Write the increasing step
function as its first value plus its **nonnegative** successive
increments times the indicators of the upper tails. Bound each tail
by \(B_i\) and collect terms to get \(S_j\). This never subtracts
two upper bounds on actual zero counts. The low real-part zeros
use the \(L^2/16\) bound above, and the formula proves \(|e(L)|\le D_j(L)\).

BS=[]
for i in range(2400,2800):
    u=B(i).r
    BS.append(min(u,BS[-1]) if BS else u)
END=[2800,2700]
def spec(j):
    end=END[j];bs=BS[:end-2400]
    return [(1-I(i)/3200,I(u)-v) for i,u,v in zip(range(2401,end+1),bs,bs[1:]+[Q(0)]) if u!=v]
SPECT=[spec(j) for j in (0,1)]
# To evaluate across many cells, share one common power table per argument.
@lru_cache(maxsize=15000)
def ds(L):
    L=I(L); w=(-L/3200).exp()
    acc=I(0); head=I(0)
    x0=w**800
    for i in range(2400,2800):
        x0/=w
        v=(I(BS[i-2400])-BS[i-2399])*x0 if i<2799 else I(0)
        if i==2699: head=acc+BS[i-2400]*x0
        acc+=v
    base=Q('2.091')*L*(-L/3).exp()+L**2/16*(-L/4).exp()
    return base+acc+BS[-1]*x0,base+head

For a stronger whole-domain profile replace \(S_j\) by
\[

        \inf_{.75\le r\le s}B_{\rm int}(r)\,ds .              \tag{S5}
\]
This follows by writing the exponential on each zero as a constant
plus the integral of its nonnegative derivative up to that zero.
It is no larger than the mesh majorant. The running infimum within a
row is the min of that row's value and the values at earlier row-ends taken from the left (S2
decreases in each row). The integrals admit ordinary positive
quadrature with bounds or S3 order-3/4 brackets; no sampled
interpolation is needed for validity. In particular
\(\limsup_{L\to\infty} e^{a_jL}|e(L)|\le B_{\rm int}(b_j)\):
split the integral at \(b_j-\epsilon\) to see this immediately.
Bounds from S3 are .010444096 and .146302424, respectively, not claims of
optimal constants for primes.

Let \(C(L)=\lambda+113.67e^{-L/2}\). CH2 Cor. 1.2 (PDF p.3 text
190–240) at \(T=H\) gives \(|e|\le C\) when \(e^L>H\), using
\(1\le y\coth y\le1+y^2/3,\ y=\pi/H\) and
\(\pi/(H-1)+\pi^2/(3H^2)\le\lambda\).
The square-root coefficient is directly checked in bounds.py.
For each \(10^7\le T\le H,\ e^L>\max(T,10^9)\), retain the original
*signed* interval centered at \((\pi/T)\coth(\pi/T)-1\) with radius
\(\pi/(T-1)+c(T)e^{-L/2}\), where
\(c(T)=([\log(T/(2\pi))]^2-\log(T/(2\pi))/3)/(2\pi)\).
Its symmetric counterpart has the additional constant
\(\pi^2/(3T^2)\). CH2 Cor. 1.3 applies on \(x\ge1\), including below \(H\).

source_references.full_readback:
absolutely convergent identity is
\[
 K(L)=\sum_\rho\frac{e^{(\rho-1)L}}{\rho(\rho-1)}
          -\log(2\pi)e^{-L}
          +\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{e^{-(2m+1)L}}{2m(2m+1)}.        \tag{S7}
\]
To prove it, integrate \(A(s)x^{s-1}/[s(s-1)]\) on \(\Re s=2\)
with \(ds/(2\pi i)\), where \(A=-\zeta'/\zeta\). The absolutely
convergent Dirichlet series can be integrated term by term. The
kernel is \(x^{-1}(x/n-1)_+\) by closing the contour using poles
0 and 1 (at equality it is 0). The integral equals
\(G(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)(1/n-1/x)\). Partial summation and
\(\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)/n-\log x\to-\gamma_{\!E}\) give
\(G=L-1-\gamma_{\!E}-K(L)\); the normalization follows by adding
the convergent prime-power series to Dusart Theorem 5.7.

Shift first to the vertical line \(\Re s=-2m-1\) for fixed \(m\ge1\).
At arbitrarily large positive and negative heights away from all nearby
zero ordinates by \(\gg1/\log |t|\) the horizontal integrals vanish.
Indeed each interval \([N-2,N+3]\) has \(O(\log N)\) ordinates by FKS's
zero count; remove intervals of sufficiently small reciprocal-log
length to find a height in \([N,N+1]\). CH2 Prop. B.8 (PDF p.46,
text 6744–6819), \(a=1,\sigma_+=2\), gives \(O(\log^2|t|)\) for the
logarithmic derivative uniformly on \([-2,2]\). To the left use
CH2 Lemma A.4 (PDF p.41), Euler convergence for \(1-s\), and the
digamma integral in the proof of their Lemma A.1. The same digamma
integral (bounded kernel) and the cotangent bound \(|\cot(\pi s/2)|\le1\)
on the negative odd vertical line give \(O(1+\log(2m+|t|+2))\) there.
The denominator is at least \((2m+1)^2+t^2\) in magnitude, so the
vertical integral tends to zero as \(m\to\infty\) for \(x>1\).
Zero residues converge absolutely by the count. At 1 the residue
is \(L-1-\gamma_{\!E}\); at 0 it is \((\zeta'/\zeta)(0)e^{-L}
=\log(2\pi)e^{-L}\) by (A.3) (the pole terms and the Euler constants
cancel). At each zero the residue is the negative of that zero's
term in S7. This proves S7 on the real ray, without exchanging a
conditionally convergent unsmoothed formula with an integral.

at 1:
\(\sum_\rho1/[\rho(1-\rho)]=2+\gamma_{\!E}-\log(4\pi)<.047\).

digamma function (differentiate the Euler limit for Gamma, and
sum the integer/half-integer harmonic differences). Each summand
has positive real part, since \(\Re(\rho(1-\rho))>0\). For the low
half-line zeros it is positive real and equals \(1/|\rho(\rho-1)|\).

the numerical constant with the harmonic enclosure of width 1/10000.

for \(t\ge100\): the required \(7/8+R(t)\) comparison holds at 100,
and divided by \(t\) its left side decreases while the right side
increases. Tonelli yields \(2\sum_{\gamma>H}\gamma^{-2}\le
4(h+1)/(5H)<8\cdot10^{-12}\). Finally the trivial-zero terms are

A stronger option on many compact domains uses the full finite-RH height.
Set \(v=Y+\log2.45\), \(W_+=\max(0,v-h)\),
\(R(h)=.137h+.443\log h+1.588\) (Rosser radius in log units), and
\[
 c_H^*=\frac1{2\pi}+\frac{.137h+.443}{Hh(h-\log(2\pi))}.
\]
Use the sharper majorant
\[
 d_{\rm split,j}=
 e^{-a_jL}\{2.091+2[c_H^* W_+((v+h)/2-\log(2\pi))+2R(h)/H]\}
 +[1.4+.17(h+1)(h+2)]e^{-L/2}.
\]
Indeed all low zeros through \(H\) are on the half line; the
bound for their reciprocals follows by limiting FKS Cor. 2.3
from \(V>H\). Above \(H\), if \(V=2.45T>H\), bound the
reciprocals by \(2 B_1(H,V)\) from FKS (2.1), taking \(V\)
from above for closed boundaries. If \(V\le H\) this sum
vanishes and we may use the nonnegative formula shown. Both
new bounds are valid on the whole ray \(L\ge40\), separately
for each \(j\). B1 can always retain any stronger B0 branch,
so the envelope is nested even if particular height choices
are not optimized or nested.

the same row data and running minima, including the artificial

# Quarter original bin width, positive increments with the same source constants.
def new_table():
    bs=[]; ri=0
    for r in range(9600,11200):
        while ri+1<len(rows) and rows[ri+1][0]*4<=r:ri+=1
        _,c,d=rows[ri]
        s=I(r)/12800
        aa=(8*s-5)/3;q=5-2*s
        sm=term=I(1)
        for k in range(1,5):
            term*=(q-k+1)/(aa*h);sm+=term
        val=2*(I(c)*(q*h.ln()-aa*h).exp()/aa*sm+I(d)*(h*h+2*h+2)/H)
        bs.append(min(val.r,bs[-1]) if bs else val.r)
    return bs
BS4=new_table()

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def d_fine(x,j):
    L=I(x); end=1200 if j else 1600
    w=(-L/12800).exp(); pw=w**(3200-end)
    # Sum positive coefficients, Horner from the lower end.
    v=I(0)
    for i in range(end-1):
        v=v*w+(I(BS4[i])-BS4[i+1])
    v=v*w+BS4[end-1]
    return v*pw+Q('2.091')*L*(-L/3).exp()+L**2/16*(-L/4).exp()

source_references.full_readback:
The extra derivative factor in the partial-summation estimate
of M4 is avoidable. For \(L\ge\log2\) write \(K\) from S7 as
an absolutely convergent exponential expansion with terms
\(c_z e^{-zu}\), \(\Re z>0\) (for zeros \(z=1-\rho\)).
For real \(t\ge0\), integrate by parts using \(-K'=e\):
\[
 \int_L^\infty e(u)e^{-tu}\,du
   = \sum_z c_z e^{-(z+t)L}\frac{z}{z+t}.
\]
Here we integrate \(K\), not its termwise derivative.
Absolute convergence at \(L\) permits the interchange for
\(t>0\); at \(t=0\) the formula is \(K(L)\).
The multiplier satisfies \(|z/(z+t)|\le1\).
For \(W(u)=1/u+1/u^2=\int_0^\infty(1+t)e^{-tu}dt\)
another absolute interchange is valid by integrability of the
scalar majorants (also directly using S1 for the initial
left-hand integral). Hence
\[
 \left|\int_L^\infty e(u)W(u)\,du\right|\le W(L) k_j(L).
\]
This holds also for any of the tighter **absolute sum**
budgets for S7. In M4 one can therefore delete the
\((1/L+2/L^2)J_k\) term in the numerator of \(V\).
The exact Mertens interval recipe can retain this new
integral enclosure whenever it supplies a smaller interval;
the \(A\)/weighted channel is unchanged. This is a strict
algebraic improvement of the scalar M4 log radius
throughout its applicable ray, not a promise that it
strictly beats all other branches everywhere. The checks in
§§1–3 conservatively used the older M4, so remain valid.

source_references.full_readback:
Put \(n=38358837682,\ A=1644673232,\ B=632207037\).
The last real failure is the unique root \(r\) in \((n,n+1)\) of
\[
    e\,r B/\log r=A^2.
\]
The independently certified bracket is
\[
 38358837682.217926<r<38358837682.217927.
\]
In particular \(R(x)>0\) for **all real \(x>r\)**, and this strict
ray cannot start at or to the left of \(r\). The last integer
failure is \(n\); the closed integer ray starts at \(n+1\).
Equality holds at \(r\).

Evidence: bounds.py endpoint uses exact falling-floor prime counting.
Start with counts \(s(v)=v-1\) for the distinct positive
\(v=\lfloor N/i\rfloor\). On detecting a prime \(p\) by
\(s(p)>s(p-1)\), for descending \(v\ge p^2\) subtract
\(s(\lfloor v/p\rfloor)-s(p-1)\). These are the remaining integers
with least prime factor \(p\), of the form \(p k\), \(k\ge p\).
Closure of the quotient set under \(v\mapsto\lfloor v/p\rfloor\)
and the decreasing update order make this an exact sieve; at the
end only primes remain. It gives \(\pi(n)=A\) and
\(\pi(14111427770)=B\). Both \(n/e\) and \((n+1)/e\) have floor
14111427770. Thus both counts on \([n,n+1)\) are as specified,
and there the coefficient \(ex/\log x\) is continuous strictly
increasing. Directed computation gives \(R(n)<-14736927\) and the
strict sign tests at the displayed bracket.

The inherited finite integer input is the integer portion of PT
2021, Theorem 2 (arXiv:1809.03134v2 PDF p.3, lines 205–212):
from \(n+1\) through the last integer at most \(e^{58}\).
Its printed lower-range statement, if read literally as **real**
\(n<x\le e^{58}\), is false: the left bracket endpoint above is an
explicit counterexample. Its finite integer portion, not the
incorrect real endpoint, is used here at original literature trust.
For \(x\ge n+1\) through \(e^{58}\), \(\pi(x)=\pi(\lfloor x\rfloor)\),
while \(ex/\log x\) and \(\pi(x/e)\) are nondecreasing, so the integer
claim extends to these reals. At \(e^{58}\) the new analytic ray
already applies and there is no upper join gap. Dudek–Platt
(arXiv:1407.1901v1) gives the same last integer candidate (intro,
PDF p.2, lines 45–55; computation, p.8, lines 591–594); its
Theorem 1.3 for all integers is conditional on full RH and is not
used as such. The new proof replaces the old analytic thresholds
\(e^{3915}\) (PT 2021) and \(e^{9658}\) (Dudek–Platt Thm. 1.2).
The input-independent sign onset is already sharp, so the extra
assumption cannot improve it.

def pi_count(n):
    m=isqrt(n)
    v=list(dict.fromkeys(n//i for i in range(1,m+1)))
    v+=list(range(min(m,v[-1]-1),0,-1))
    s={u:u-1 for u in v}
    for p in range(2,m+1):
        b=s[p-1]
        if s[p]==b: continue
        for u in v:
            if u<p*p: break
            s[u]-=s[u//p]-b
    return s[n]

def endpoint():
    n=38358837682
    a,b=I(n)/E,I(n+1)/E
    assert int(a.l)==int(b.r)==14111427770
    p,q=pi_count(n),pi_count(int(a.l))
    assert (p,q)==(1644673232,632207037)
    def gap(x):
        return E*x/x.ln()*q-p*p
    assertlt(gap(I(n)),0)
    l,r=I('38358837682.217926'),I('38358837682.217927')
    assertlt(gap(l),0);assertlt(0,gap(r))
    print('endpoint',p,q,gap(I(n)),l,r,flush=True)

Let \(P(L)=\sum_{q=0}^{20}q!/L^q\), \(\Xi(L)=L e^{-L}\pi(e^L)\), and
\(F(x)=2/\log 2+\int_2^x dt/\log t\). This last reference avoids
any ambiguity about the normalization of li. For \(L\ge30\),
\[
 P(L)\le Le^{-L}F(e^L)\le P(L)+v(L),\quad
 v(L)=10Le^{-L}+\tfrac{15}4\,21!\,L^{-21}.                    \tag{R2}
\]
At 30, \(F(e^{30})-e^{30}P(30)/30\) is in (0,10): integrate
the positive series for \(e^u/u\) starting at \(\log2\) and
bound its tail geometrically after term 180. It is about 9.124.
The derivative of the difference is \(21!e^L/L^{22}\), and the
log derivative of \(e^L/L^{22}\) is at least \(1-22/30=4/15\)
on this ray. Integrating proves R2. No asymptotic expansion is
being used as a convergent infinite series.

# F(exp(30)) by convergent elementary series, tail < 10^-50.
    def se(v):
        a=I(1);s=I(0)
        for n in range(1,181):
            a=a*v/n;s+=a/n
        return s
    a=I(30)
    val=2/LN2+(a/LN2).ln()+se(a)-se(LN2)+I('-1e-50','1e-50')-a.exp()/a*P(a)
    # tail at 30: use geometric ratio < 1/6 after n=180 (ratio 30/181).
    assertlt(I(30)**181/I(factorial(181))/181*I(6)/5,Q('1e-50'))
    assertlt(0,val); assertlt(val,10)
    print('main constants OK, anchor',val,flush=True)

source_references.full_readback:
**Signed refinement.** At \(L\ge34\) use
\[
 d_j=\min\{C,\ F_\psi\ (34\le L\le58),\ D_j\ (L\ge40)\},
\]
and \(V=.9999e^{-L/2}\le(\psi(e^L)-\theta(e^L))e^{-L}\)
from Dusart Prop. 4.3. Integration by parts using \(e(u)=-K'(u)\)
a.e. bounds the contribution of the \(\psi\) error to the part of
the R3 integral from 20 onwards by the terminal \(k_j(L)/L\),
a term from the endpoint 20, and
\[
 Le^{-L}\int_{20}^L e^u(1/u^2-2/u^3) k_j(u)\,du.
\]
Together with the initial **theta** integral through 20 this is
bounded in absolute value by
\[
 J_j(L)=\frac{.1645e^{-L/2}
      +8\cdot10^{-12}(1+1/(.9-a_j))e^{-a_jL}
      +1.838e^{-L}+e^{-3L}}{L}+3104Le^{-L}.
\]
For \(a=.5,a_j\) use the log-derivative bound just proved;
the two other integrated terms and the endpoint at 20 are
bounded by \(Le^{-L}\) times
\(1.838/20+e^{-40}/800+e^{20}k_j(20)/400<4\).
In (R3) the drift is **subtracted** at the endpoint and in the
remaining integral. For an upper bound keep just its lower
endpoint \(V\); for a lower bound bound both pieces by
\(U_2=1.000001(1+2.5/L)e^{-L/2}+1.78(1+30/(7L))e^{-2L/3}\).
Thus the positive upper error and lower-error magnitude can be
taken as
\[
 u_j=\max(0,\min(b_j,d_j+J_j-V)),\qquad
 w_j=\min(b_j,d_j+J_j+U_2).                                  \tag{R4}
\]
The signed finite \(\pi<\operatorname{li}\) input furthermore
allows \(u_j=0\) through \(x=1.2\cdot10^{17}\).

def psi_bound(L,j,early):
    L=I(L)
    u=A_C(L)
    if early and L.l>=34:
        u=imin(u,((L-2*(L/(PI*E)).ln())**2-4)/(8*PI)*(-L/2).exp())
    if L.l>=40:
        u=imin(u,ds(L.l)[j])
    return u

@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def improved_parts(L,j,early):
    l=I(L)
    a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    J=(Q('.1645')*(-l/2).exp()+Q('8e-12')*(1+1/(Q('.9')-a))*(-a*l).exp()
        +Q('1.838')*(-l).exp()+(-3*l).exp())/l +3104*l*(-l).exp()
    drift=(Q('1.000001')*(1+Q('2.5')/l)*(-l/2).exp()
           +Q('1.78')*(1+I(30)/7/l)*(-2*l/3).exp())
    u=psi_bound(l,j,early)+J
    return u,u+drift

def two_errors(l,r,j):
    lo,hi=I(l),I(r)
    up,_=improved_parts(l,j,r<=58)
    _,dn=improved_parts(F.subtract(l,Q(1)),j,r<=59)
    pp=Q('.9999')*(-hi/2).exp()
    return (I(0,max(Q(0),imin(ub(l,j,r<=58),up-pp).r)),
            upper(imin(ub(F.subtract(l,Q(1)),j,r<=59),dn)))

Set, for \(0\le i\le36\), \(q=i+4\) and
\[
 c_i=\sum_{k=0}^{\min(20,q)}k!\binom{q}{k}
       -\sum_{k=\max(0,q-20)}^{\min(20,q)}k!(q-k)! .
\]
For all \(L\ge35\) a strict profile is
\[
 G>\sum_{i=0}^{36}c_i L^{-i}
       -L^4\left[{L\over L-1}w_j(L-1)
              +z_j(L)(2P(L)+z_j(L))\right],\qquad z_j=v+u_j.  \tag{R5}
\]
One can also use \(u_j=w_j=b_j\) and take the max with that result,
or use continuous S5 in the pointwise formulas. Indeed
\(G=L^4[(L/(L-1))\Xi(L-1)-\Xi(L)^2]\). In the main-term
difference involving \(P\), the coefficients at degrees 0–3
in \(1/L\) cancel exactly; the displayed formula computes through
degree 40. The omitted terms in the first summand are all
positive, and the square has degree 40, proving strictness
without relying on strictly rounded prime error bounds. For a
still tighter pointwise result one can use the exact rational
main expression \(L^4[(L/(L-1))P(L-1)-P(L)^2]\), using R5 as
the convenient strict certificate. These profiles retain the
higher-order terms even where an individual constant-margin
row does not apply.

def ram_row(k,m,u,j,f,signed):
    m,u=Q(m),Q(u); d=k+(m==cs[k]); T=Q(450 if k<=8 else 650); t=I(T)
    assert d+6 < (T-1)/8 and d+4 < 21
    assertlt(loss(t,t,primeB(T,j,f),primeB(T-1,j,f),d)+sum(-c/t**(i-d) for i,c in enumerate(cs) if c<0),
             cs[d]-(0 if d>k else m))
    def part(l,r):
        p,q=I(l),I(r)
        ub,wb=errors(l,r,j,f,signed)
        if (resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,ub,wb,k)).l>m:return 1
        assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,k,j,m,resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,ub,wb,k))
        mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
        return part(l,mid)+part(mid,r)
    ends=[u]+[Q(t) for t in [34,35,40,41,58,59,80,125,166,169,189,190,230,300,375] if u<t<T]+[T]
    return sum(part(l,r) for l,r in zip(ends,ends[1:]))

**Whole-domain certification.** For R1 multiply (R5) after
subtracting the prefix by \(L^k\). On each certificate cell
\([l,r]\) bound positive main coefficients at \(r\) and negative
ones at \(l\); for the loss take the powers of \(L\) at \(r\),
the factor \(L/(L-1)\), \(P,v\), and decreasing errors at \(l\)
(with \(l-1\) where appropriate). In the signed upper error
use the subtractive \(V\) at \(r\). All decreasing factors are
positive exponential polynomials, or inverse powers, except
the finite S6 expression: its log derivative is negative
on \([34,58]\) since the polynomial factor has log derivative
less than .1, as seen from \(L-2\log(L/(\pi e))>30\) and
its derivative \(1-2/L\). The cells split at applicability
boundaries, including their shifts by 1. At 58 and 59 the
following cell may simply use the bounds not needing the
finite branch. The finite signed bridge is checked slightly
past its last log endpoint for the numerical expression only,
then used just up to the allowed original \(x\). It overlaps
the analytic .16 ray starting at 39.32. Every accepted cell
is a proof, not a test at a sample point.

For \(L\ge450\), use \(b_D\) (or the corresponding fallback).
Each term of the scaled loss, and the dropped negative
coefficients, is nonincreasing there: for the exponent power
\(d=k+4\) or \(k+5\), use \((d+2)/(L-1)<1/8\), and
\(d<21\) for the inverse-power remainder; \(L/(L-1)\) and
\(P\) are decreasing. The code verifies at 450 that this
loss plus all absolute negative terms is below \(c_k-m\).
When \(m=c_k\), instead scale by one extra \(L\) and compare
to \(c_{k+1}\). No finite-ray check is substituted for this
tail argument; all onsets and finite joins are inclusive.

def ram():
    A=Q('450')
    def verify(k,m,a,j,improved=False,fallback=False):
        a,m=Q(a),Q(m)
        d=k+(m==cs[k])
        t=I(A)
        assert d+6 < (A-1)/8
        assertlt(loss(t,t,bD(A,j,fallback),bD(A-1,j,fallback),d)+sum(-c/t**(i-d) for i,c in enumerate(cs) if c<0),
                 cs[d]-(0 if d>k else m))
        if a>=A:return
        cells=0
        def part(l,r):
            nonlocal cells
            p,q=I(l),I(r)
            if improved:
                up,dn=two_errors(l,r,j)
            else:
                up,dn=ub(l,j,r<=58,fallback),ub(F.subtract(l,Q(1)),j,r<=59,fallback)
            lower=resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,up,dn,k)
            if lower.l>m:
                cells+=1;return
            assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,k,j,m,lower)
            mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
            part(l,mid);part(mid,r)
        ends=[a]+[Q(t) for t in [34,35,40,41,58,59,80,125,166,169,189,190,230,300,375] if a<t<A]+[A]
        for l,r in zip(ends,ends[1:]): part(l,r)
        return cells

def ram():
    A=Q('450')
    def verify(k,m,a,j,improved=False,fallback=False):
        a,m=Q(a),Q(m)
        d=k+(m==cs[k])
        t=I(A)
        assert d+6 < (A-1)/8
        assertlt(loss(t,t,bD(A,j,fallback),bD(A-1,j,fallback),d)+sum(-c/t**(i-d) for i,c in enumerate(cs) if c<0),
                 cs[d]-(0 if d>k else m))
        if a>=A:return
        cells=0
        def part(l,r):
            nonlocal cells
            p,q=I(l),I(r)
            if improved:
                up,dn=two_errors(l,r,j)
            else:
                up,dn=ub(l,j,r<=58,fallback),ub(F.subtract(l,Q(1)),j,r<=59,fallback)
            lower=resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,up,dn,k)
            if lower.l>m:
                cells+=1;return
            assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,k,j,m,lower)
            mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
            part(l,mid);part(mid,r)
        ends=[a]+[Q(t) for t in [34,35,40,41,58,59,80,125,166,169,189,190,230,300,375] if a<t<A]+[A]
        for l,r in zip(ends,ends[1:]): part(l,r)
        return cells
    for k,m,a,b in ROWS:
        t0=verify(k,m,a,0);t1=verify(k,m,b,1)
        print('onset',k,m,a,b,t0,t1,flush=True)
    for k,a,m0,m1 in FIXED:
        print('fixed',k,a,m0,m1,verify(k,m0,a,0),verify(k,m1,a,1),flush=True)

def signed_bridge():
    # At x up to 1.2e17 the Dudek--Platt proof gives pi(x) < li(x) < F(x).
    # The constants of both li normalizations used by the corpus are below F.
    top=I(120*10**15).ln()
    B=top.r
    def check(a,m):
        def part(l,r):
            p,q=I(l),I(r)
            _,d=two_errors(l,r,0)
            out=resmain(p,q,0)-loss(p,q,I(0),d,0)
            if out.l>Q(m):return 1
            assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,m,out)
            mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
            return part(l,mid)+part(mid,r)
        print('signed bridge',a,m,part(Q(a),B),flush=True)
    for a,m in [('36.55','0'),('36.64','.05'),('36.75','.1'),
                ('36.88','.16'),('36.98','.2'),('39','.8')]:
        check(a,m)
    assertlt(I('39.32'),top)
    assertlt(I('36.55').exp(),115*10**14)

source_references.full_readback:
More strongly, retain the actual numerical functions of PT
(19),(20) at its published anchor \(U=\log x_a=3914\) (PDF
pp.10–11, text 889–985), i.e., the originally printed coefficients
\(M_a(L),m_a(L)\). For this comparison \(a\) is just the numerical
piecewise function of their (18), including its false first
piece: **do not** use it as a \(\theta\) estimate at small input.
Let \(P_4(L)=\sum_{i=0}^4 i!/L^i\). The existing density-free
R2–R3 and \(b_D^*\) of ramanujan.md prove
\[
 120 < L^5(\Xi(L)-P_4(L)) <120+.19\qquad(L\ge U).
\]
For the lower bound use \(L^6 b_D^*<720\); for the upper use
\(\sum_{i=6}^{20}i!L^{5-i}+L^5(b_D^*+v)<.19\).
All needed terms after scaling are decreasing on this ray
(positive powers in exponentials are dominated by their decay),
and the checks at \(U\) appear in repair.py. The same
upper bound holds for the smooth \(Le^{-L}F(e^L)\) without \(b_D^*\).
Write \(B=1/U+196/U^2\); the bracket in (19),(20) is at least
\(B\) (also under the power-of-two reading in the flattened text).
Clearly \(M_a\ge120+720B>120+.19\), since \(C_1,a\ge0\).

To handle \(m_a\), bound
\[
 -C_2\le U^6 e^{-U}\int_{\log2}^{U}e^u\,a(e^u)/u^7\,du
 \ < 1100 U^6 e^{-114}+\frac{a(x_a)}{.99 U}
 \ < a(x_a)B .
\]
For \(u\le3800\), each printed \(a(e^u)/u^5\) is less than
500: the first piece is <1; maximize \(u^2e^{-u/2}\) at 4 for
the second; for the third use \(u/6.455<1169/6.455<500\)
(with the fourth-root and decaying factors); for the remaining
pieces maximize \(v^{3.04}e^{-1.89v}\) over \(v>0\) at
\(v=3.04/1.89\), using coefficient at most 462. Divide by
\(u^2\) and use \(500/(\log2)^2<1100\).
For \(3800\le u\le U\), the log derivative of the integrand is
\(1-.48/u-1.89/(2\sqrt{5.573412u})\), which is \(>.99\)
(the .48/u allowance is needed in this test).
The final comparison is directed in repair.py. Thus \(m_a\le120\),
since \(C_3,a\ge0\). This validates the actual optional interval
with coefficients \(m_a,M_a\) on log-domain \([3914,\infty)\)
without relying on the false auxiliary estimate. It does not
assert a theorem for arbitrary anchors/formulas. For use at
both Ramanujan arguments its common log-onset is 3915.

## 3. Strict envelope comparisons, now from \(L=168.745\)

The radius floor \(f_0=\min(1.046\cdot10^{-12},.0104e^{-L/8})\)
of mertens.md §5 still works on this slightly enlarged domain.
The source constants and monotonic ratios justify the same
comparisons (on the plateau use through 190 as before);
for the refined B0 mesh its terminal coefficient exceeds
.0104 by the directed check. The two new density-free bounds
each include \(2.091e^{-L/8}\), so do not invalidate the floor.
The S5 and old signed \(K\) alternatives have the same
budget and centers. The new kernel option in §4 below adds
an interval containing 0 for its integral on this ray
(even if the elementary terms are separated as a signed
center: one may bound them by the stated symmetric radius,
and the half-line budget exceeds their magnitude; the
explicit preexisting signed-center variants use only S7/S8).
As before, loss of radius by signed prime powers is at most
\(3e^{-L/2}\) in scaled units. The new checks verify
\(LV/(1-V)< F_*(L)\) for \(L=168.745\), with
\(F_*=\min(1.045\cdot10^{-12},.01e^{-L/8})\) and
\(d=d_{\rm fine,1}\), and both ratios decrease on the ray.
The signed upper \(\pi\)-error before drift subtraction is
also less than both defining quantities of \(F_*\) at the
left endpoint, with the same declining ratios thereafter.
Thus the strict Mertens improvement holds on this enlarged
ray, and so does the strict R4–R5 improvement. No strict
gain on every point before this ray is asserted; B1 retains
all old bounds regardless.

For the original direct \(\pi\) branches in ramanujan.md,
one can now certify strict improvement of the *combined*
pointwise Ramanujan portfolio on this ray. Use the exact
smooth center \(\Xi_F=Le^{-L}F(e^L)\) in R3–R5, rather than
its finite polynomial lower and upper approximations: the
approximations were only for certification of table rows.
The old constructed upper endpoints before adding \(\Xi_F\)
are at least \(f_0-.9999e^{-L/2}>F_*\); the new construction
is strictly inside that. Each retained direct original-source
upper endpoint also exceeds \(\Xi_F+f_0\):
* For Dusart 5.1, R2 implies \(\Xi_F<P_2+6.3/L^3\).
  Check at 168.745 and use termwise decrease after scaling by
  \(L^3\). Thus the 7.32 (or 7.59) upper coefficient leaves
  more than \(1/L^3>f_0\): check through the plateau to 190,
  then use the increasing ratio to \(e^{-L/8}\). Here
  \(P_2=1+1/L+2/L^2\). For Cor. 5.2–5.3 the uppers are
  at least \(P_2+7.32/L^3\) by direct algebra. In particular,
  for the second rational upper expand the difference from
  \(P_2\) via \(y=1/L,\ c=1.2311\): its numerator is
  \((c-1)y^2+(c+2)y^3+2cy^4\), with positive denominator
  \(1-y-cy^2<1\); the first rational upper is at least
  \(1+1.112/L\). The remaining polynomial comparisons check
  at the left endpoint with decreasing inverse powers.
* For PT Cor. 2, the normalized radius
  \(235 L^{1.52}e^{-.8\sqrt L}\) exceeds twice both the
  center translation \((2/\log2)Le^{-L}\) and \(f_0\)
  from its own onset 2000. These ratios increase by direct
  logarithmic differentiation (replace \(f_0\) by its
  power part).
* The PT (19) published-anchor upper has distance
  \(>.002/L^5\) above \(\Xi_F\) on \(L\ge3914\) by repair.md
  and \(720B>.192\); again the ratio to the power branch of
  \(f_0\) increases (and is checked at 3914).

The stronger unshifted upper bound is strictly positive
(it bounds a nonzero prime count), so its square strictly
decreases. For the shifted lower, use B1's nonstrict
improvement from retaining all B0 options. This proves strict
improvement of the combined constructed/direct-source
lower profile, not an optimality assertion about all proofs
from B0. At these logs the sign-only finite theorem supplies
no stronger margin than the positive constructed profile.
All quantitative rows only certify subprofiles from their
underlying inequalities (or their maxima), so retaining those
rows cannot spoil this comparison.

L=I('168.745')
        z=mert_point(L.l,1,d_fine)
        p=signed_part(L.l,1,False,d_fine)[0]
        for q in (I('1.045e-12'),Q('.01')*(-L/8).exp()):
            assertlt(z,q);assertlt(p,q)
        for q in (I('1e-15'),Q('.0004')*(-L/8).exp()):

            assertlt(signed_part(L.l,1,False,d_split)[0],q)

        L=I('168.745')
        # Smooth Xi comparisons with all retained direct pi uppers.
        assertlt(sum(I(factorial(k))/L**(k-3) for k in range(3,21))+L**3*err(L),Q('6.3'))
        assertlt(Q('7.32')/L**3,Q('.53816')/L**2)
        assertlt(1/L+2/L**2+Q('7.32')/L**3,Q('.2551'))
        assertlt(2/L+Q('7.32')/L**2,Q('.112'))
        assertlt(Q('7.32')/L,Q('.2311'))
        assertlt(I('1e-12')+I('4.6e-14'),1/I(190)**3)
        assertlt(Q('.0104')*(-I(190)/8).exp(),1/I(190)**3)
        t=I(2000)

All endpoints in this file are for **reals**, inclusive unless
specified, with sums over \(p\le x\). Write \(\gamma_{\!E}\) for Euler's
constant and take the constants of Dusart Theorems 5.6 and 5.7 exactly:
\[
 M=\gamma_{\!E}+\sum_p(\log(1-1/p)+1/p),\qquad
 B_3=\gamma_{\!E}+\sum_{m\ge2}\sum_p(\log p)p^{-m}.
\]
Set \(Z_{\rm raw}=\log Q_{\rm raw}-\gamma_{\!E}-\log L\),
\(E_1=\sum1/p-\log L-M\), and \(E_\ell=\sum(\log p)/p-L+B_3\).
The two relative product errors are \(|e^{-Z_{\rm raw}}-1|\)
and \(|e^{Z_{\rm raw}}-1|\).

Let
\[
 A=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)/n-L+\gamma_{\!E},\qquad
 Z=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)/(n\log n)-\log L-\gamma_{\!E},
 \qquad W(u)=1/u+1/u^2 .
\]
The limits after subtracting \(L\) and \(\log L\) follow from
Dusart 5.7 and 5.6 by adding the appropriate absolutely convergent
prime-power sums. Stieltjes partial summation, followed by
integration by parts with the absolutely continuous \(K\) of S7,
gives
\[
 A=e(L)-K(L),\quad Z=e(L)/L-\int_L^\infty e(u)W(u)\,du,\quad
 \int_L^\infty e(u)W(u)\,du=W(L)K(L)+\int_L^\infty K(u)W'(u)\,du .
                                                               \tag{M2}
\]
These formulas hold with jumps at \(x\) included in the endpoint
sums. Crucially the integral costs \(k_j\), not a new multiple
of the principal bound \(d\) for \(|e|\). The naive approach
\(\int |e|\le d/a\) would cost a factor close to \(1+1/a\).

For \(L\ge18\),
\[
 C_\ell\le1.34e^{-L/2},\qquad C_P\le C_1\le1.34e^{-L/2}/L.
                                                               \tag{M3}
\]
The same bounds with 1.37 work for \(L\ge17.8\).
For the square term use \(\theta(y)=y+O(3.965\,y/\log^2 y)\)
at \(y=e^{L/2}\) (Dusart Thm. 4.2), and the tail integration
rule in §4. Relative to \(e^{-L/2}\), or \(e^{-L/2}/L\) for
\(C_1\), the bound is \(1+(4\cdot3.965/L^2)(3+2/L)\)
(the weighted case needs only 3). For \(3\le m\le M'=\lfloor L/\log2\rfloor\)
use the bound \(\theta(t)\le1.000081t\) stated in Dusart's proof
of Prop. 4.4 (PDF p.13). Discarding the nonpositive endpoint
in the integral, the coefficient at \(e^{-(1-1/m)L}\)
for the weighted sum, or at \(e^{-(1-1/m)L}/L\) for \(C_1\),
is at most \(1.000081\,(m/(m-1))(1+1/L)\).
Sum \(m=3,\ldots,7\) individually and bound all \(m\ge8\)
through \(M'\) by \(L/\log 2\) terms with relative exponential
\(e^{-3L/8}\). For \(m>M'\) use the same \(\theta\) upper bound
integrated from \(2^{-}\), giving total weighted
\(\le3.001\,2^{-M'}<6.002/x\). For \(C_1\) each is further
divided by \(m\log2>L\). This gives pp_check in bounds.py;
every summand in the scaled bound decreases on the stated
rays, so its directed check at the left endpoint suffices.

assertlt(pp_check(18),Q('1.34'))
    assertlt(pp_check('17.8'),Q('1.37'))

With \(J_k(L)=\int_L^\infty k_j(u)\,du\), \(p(L)=C_{\rm pp}e^{-L/2}\)
from (M3), and any valid \(d\ge|e(L)|\), define
\[
 U=d+k_j+p,\qquad
 V=\big[d+(1+1/L)k_j+(1/L+2/L^2)J_k+p\big]/L.                 \tag{M4}
\]
Then \(|E_\ell|\le U,\ |E_1|,|Z_{\rm raw}|\le V\).
This uses that \(|W'|\) decreases. For the products take
\(e^V-1\) or the convenient \(V/(1-V)\) when \(V<1\).
For (M1) use \(d=D_j\) and \(C_{\rm pp}=1.34\).
Each component of \(e^{a_jL}U\), \(e^{a_jL}LV\) and
\(1/(1-V)\) is nonincreasing for \(L\ge170\): S4 is a positive
exponential mixture, and the low terms with degrees 1 or 2
still decay after scaling. Thus the code's endpoint expression
\(e^{a_j u}uV(u)/(1-V(u))\) gives the **full ray** for any real
\(u\ge170\). The density-free alternative follows identically
after dividing by the extra \(L^2\), using S1 and \(u=300\).

def kvals(L,j):
    L=I(L);a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    return [(I('.047'),I(1)/2),(I('8e-12'),a),(I('1.838'),I(1)),(I(1),I(3))]
def ktail(L,j):
    L=I(L)
    v=[(c*(-a*L).exp(),a) for c,a in kvals(L,j)]
    return sum(c for c,a in v),sum(c/a for c,a in v)

def pp_check(a):
    L=I(a);delta=I('3.965')*4/L**2
    rest=Q('1.000081')*I('1.5')*(1+1/L)*(
        sum((-(I(1)/2-I(1)/m)*L).exp() for m in range(3,8))
        +L/LN2*(-3*L/8).exp())+Q('6.002')*(-L/2).exp()
    return 1+delta*(3+2/L)+rest

def mux(L,j,d,corr):
    # Two explicit whole-domain bounds: weighted prime sum and common
    # log-envelope for products and prime reciprocals.
    L=I(L)
    K,J=ktail(L,j)
    p=Q(corr)*(-L/2).exp()
    return d+K+p, (d+(1+1/L)*K+(1/L+2/L**2)*J+p)/L

  for \(Q\) and \(P\) respectively are
  \(\max(e^u-1,1-e^\ell)\) and \(\max(e^{-\ell}-1,1-e^{-u})\).
  For sums take the larger endpoint magnitude. Minimize each
  with the applicable old Dusart, M1/M4, early and finite
  bounds (and tighter one-sided versions if already available).
  The minima are done **pointwise**, not by comparing average
  performance on a test grid. The integrals in this specification
  converge; one can integrate only up to any chosen large
  endpoint and enclose the rest by the positive exponential
  tails of S4, S8, and M3.

def den_limit(L,j):
    # For all U>=L, exp(a*U) times the two scaled bounds of mux
    # are nonincreasing (L>=170). For products apply expm1 <= z/(1-z).
    L=I(L)
    a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    d=ds(L.l)[j]
    v,w=mux(L,j,d,'1.34')
    assert 0 <= w.l <= w.r < 1
    return v*(a*L).exp(), L*w*(a*L).exp(),L*w*(a*L).exp()/(1-w)
    l=I('168.82')
    v,w=mux(l,1,ds(l.l)[1],'1.34')
    assert 0 <= w.l <= w.r < 1
    assertlt(l*w/(1-w),Q('1.045e-12'))
    assertlt(l*w/(1-w),Q('.01')*(-l/8).exp())
    uu,_=improved_parts(l.l,1,False)
    assertlt(uu,Q('1.045e-12'))
    assertlt(uu,Q('.01')*(-l/8).exp())
    for j in (0,1):
        u=I(300);a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
        xx,zz=mux(u,j,dstar(u,j),'1.34')
        assert 0 <= zz.l <= zz.r < 1
        assertlt(xx*(a*u).exp()/u**2,Q('.0626'))
        assertlt(zz*(a*u).exp()/u/(1-zz),Q('.0626'))
    def early(k,c,z):
        k,c=Q(k),Q(c);s=Q(0);cells=0
        def part(l,r):
            p,q=I(l),I(r)
            if r<=Y.l:
                d=Q('.791')*(-p/2).exp()
            else:
                assert l>=29
                d=A_C(l)
            if l>=29:
                d=imin(d,phi_early(l),A_C(l))
            u,v=mux(p,0,d,z)
            assert 0 <= v.l <= v.r < 1
            if max((q*q*u).r,(q**3*v/(1-v)).r)<c:
                return 1
            assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(k,c,l,r,u,v)
            mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
            return part(l,mid)+part(mid,r)

def mux(L,j,d,corr):
    # Two explicit whole-domain bounds: weighted prime sum and common
    # log-envelope for products and prime reciprocals.
    L=I(L)
    K,J=ktail(L,j)
    p=Q(corr)*(-L/2).exp()
    return d+K+p, (d+(1+1/L)*K+(1/L+2/L**2)*J+p)/L

def den_limit(L,j):
    # For all U>=L, exp(a*U) times the two scaled bounds of mux
    # are nonincreasing (L>=170). For products apply expm1 <= z/(1-z).
    L=I(L)
    a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    d=ds(L.l)[j]
    v,w=mux(L,j,d,'1.34')
    assert 0 <= w.l <= w.r < 1
    return v*(a*L).exp(), L*w*(a*L).exp(),L*w*(a*L).exp()/(1-w)

def mux(L,j,d,corr):
    # Two explicit whole-domain bounds: weighted prime sum and common
    # log-envelope for products and prime reciprocals.
    L=I(L)
    K,J=ktail(L,j)
    p=Q(corr)*(-L/2).exp()
    return d+K+p, (d+(1+1/L)*K+(1/L+2/L**2)*J+p)/L

def den_limit(L,j):
    # For all U>=L, exp(a*U) times the two scaled bounds of mux
    # are nonincreasing (L>=170). For products apply expm1 <= z/(1-z).
    L=I(L)
    a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    d=ds(L.l)[j]
    v,w=mux(L,j,d,'1.34')
    assert 0 <= w.l <= w.r < 1
    return v*(a*L).exp(), L*w*(a*L).exp(),L*w*(a*L).exp()/(1-w)

for the products and \(1/p\) are at most \(C L x^{-a_j}\);

The functions \(e^{a_j L}L^{-2}U\) and

a_j+(\log L+c)/L\) decreases for \(c=1,2\); the other
nonnegative terms decrease after the same scaling. Also \(V\)
itself decreases (each \(Y+c\) has log derivative at most \(1/L\)
and \(2/L<a_j\)), so its left endpoint certificate proves
\(V<1\) everywhere needed. The constants are checked at 300;
the ratio of the new input case to the matched B0 case is

the corresponding \(\limsup\) in density-free scaling units
\(e^{a_j L}/L\) for the first three channels and
\(e^{a_j L}/L^2\) for the last is \(\le .17a_j^2\).

one wants further pointwise minimization: no shared
Perron \(T^\star\) is needed across different \(x\).

source_references.full_readback:
**Sharper density-free Mertens coefficients, same onset.**
Using \(d_{\rm split,j}\) in M4 gives \(C=.00262\) and \(.00408\)
respectively, still from \(L=300\). In scaled units the split
factor equals the sum of decreasing positive terms minus
\(c_H^*(h-\log(2\pi))^2/L^2\). In fact \(v>h\) in these ranges,
and its square contribution is
\[
 c_H^*\left(a_j+\frac{\log L+\log2.45-\log(2\pi)}{L}\right)^2
 \ -\ c_H^*\frac{(h-\log(2\pi))^2}{L^2}.
\]
The first term decreases, as do the other positive terms
of \(e^{a_jL}LV/L^2\). The unscaled \(V\) also decreases:
the maximum log derivative of the split high polynomial-log
factor is less than \(a_j\) at 300 and then decreases, by
the derivative inequality below. This verifies all signs
needed for the relative denominator at left endpoints.
On each of the 440 real cells of width 5 from 300 to 2500
use the positive part and \(1/(1-V)\) at the left and bound
the subtracted term at the right. From 2500 simply omit the
negative term, retaining a decreasing analytic bound. All
cells and the analytic left anchor are tested in advance.py.
The treatment ratio has the same decreasing \(e^{-L/32}\)
factor. The limiting coefficient improves to \(c_H^*a_j^2\)
in the same units, since logarithmic factors divided by
\(L\) vanish and the other terms are \(o(1)\).
Keep the light branch too if an entirely monotone scalar
proof with only a single arithmetic check is desired.

def d_split(x,j):
    L=I(x); Y=a(j)*L+L.ln()
    v=Y+I('2.45').ln()
    diff=v-h
    W=I(max(Q(0),diff.l),max(Q(0),diff.r))
    c=1/(2*PI)+(Q('.137')*h+Q('.443'))/(H*h*(h-(2*PI).ln()))
    rr=Q('.137')*h+Q('.443')*h.ln()+Q('1.588')
    return (Q('2.091')+2*(c*W*((v+h)/2-(2*PI).ln())+2*rr/H))*(-a(j)*L).exp()+        (Q('1.4')+Q('.17')*(h+1)*(h+2))*(-L/2).exp()
def split_m_ray(j):
    L=I(300); aa=a(j)
    v=aa*L+L.ln()+I('2.45').ln()
    log2pi=(2*PI).ln()
    assertlt(0,v-h)
    assertlt(0,v+h-2*log2pi)
    assertlt((aa+1/L)*(1/(v-h)+1/(v+h-2*log2pi)),aa)
    assertlt(1,L.ln()+I('2.45').ln()-log2pi)
    c=1/(2*PI)+(Q('.137')*h+Q('.443'))/(H*h*(h-log2pi))
    neg=c*(h-log2pi)**2
    target=Q('.00408' if j else '.00262')
    for l in range(300,2501,5):
        L=I(l); r=l+5
        _,w=mux(L,j,d_split(l,j),'1.34')
        assert 0<=w.l<=w.r<1
        # The last check drops the entire negative term for the analytic tail.
        ans=(L*w*(aa*L).exp()/L**2+neg/L**2-(0 if l==2500 else neg/I(r)**2))/(1-w)
        assertlt(ans,target)
    print('split M whole-ray',j,300,target,440,ans,flush=True)
            split_m_ray(j)
        assertlt(Q('.005563')*(-I(300)/32).exp(),Q('.003814'))
        assertlt(Q('.00408')*(-I(300)/32).exp(),Q('.00262'))

def run():
    assertlt(I('17.8').exp(),LIMIT)
    log2lo,log2hi=snap(LN2)
    logs=[snap((I(j)/4096).ln()) for j in range(4096,8192)]
    g=gamma()
    gs=snap(g)
    Mlo,Mhi=0,0
    Blo,Bhi=0,0
    plo=phi=slo=shi=tlo=thi=0
    L=[]
    critical={}
    after={912559:912560,2278379:2278383}
    n=START
    checkpoints=[]
    while n<LIMIT:
        checkpoints.append(n);n+=n//DEN
    checkpoints.append(LIMIT)
    t=iter(checkpoints)
    n=next(t)
    for p in sieve(LIMIT):
        while p>n:
            L.append((n,plo,phi,slo,shi,tlo,thi));n=next(t)
        # k*log(2)+log(j/4096)+log(1+r)
        k=p.bit_length()-1; j=(4096*p)>>k; d=j<<k; z=4096*p-d
        lower,upper=logs[j-4096]
        v=S*z//d; z2=z*z; d2=d*d
        w=S*z2//(2*d2); u=S*z2*z//(3*d2*d)
        # Alternating series, first omitted term <= 2^-50.
        lp=k*log2lo+lower+v-w+u-1-(S>>50)
        hp=k*log2hi+upper+v-w+u+2
        quot=S//p
        slo+=quot;shi+=quot+1
        tlo+=lp//p;thi+=hp//p+1
        if p<=1024:
            al,au=snap(-(1-I(1)/p).ln()-I(1)/p)
        else:
            p2=p*p;p3=p2*p;p4=p3*p;p5=p4*p;p6=p5*p
            al=S//(2*p2)+S//(3*p3)+S//(4*p4)+S//(5*p5)
            au=al+5+2*S//p6
        Mlo+=al;Mhi+=au
        plo+=quot+al;phi+=quot+au+1
        Blo+=lp//(p*(p-1));Bhi+=hp//(p*(p-1))+1
        if p in after:
            critical[p]=(fixed(plo,phi),fixed(slo,shi),fixed(tlo,thi))
        assert all(not a<p<=b for a,b in after.items())
    L.append((LIMIT,plo,phi,slo,shi,tlo,thi))
    assert len(L)==len(checkpoints)
    l=I(LIMIT).ln()
    delta=Q('.2')/l**2
    k=I(1)/(2*LIMIT)/l
    v=I(1);poly=I(1);even=None
    for n in range(1,10):
        v=-v*n/l;poly+=v
        if n==8:even=poly
    rad=k*delta*(3+1/l)
    mtail=I((k*poly-rad).l,(k*even+rad+I(1)/(LIMIT**2)).r)
    w=-(1-I(1)/LIMIT).ln()
    rad=delta*(2/I(LIMIT-1)+w)
    btail=w+I(rad.r.copy_negate(),rad.r)
    M=g-fixed(Mlo,Mhi)-mtail
    B=g+fixed(Blo,Bhi)+btail
    print('finite constants',M,B,g,flush=True)
    # Local exact earlier real thresholds for the original coefficients.
    for k,p,l,r,t in [
        (0,2278379,'2.710','2.713','.2'),
        (1,2278379,'2.574','2.577','.2'),
        (2,2278379,'3.111','3.115','.2'),
        (3,912559,'.997','.998','.3'),
    ]:
        pr,sr,wr=critical[p];tt=I(t)
        upr=I(after[p]);lpr=I(p)
        def errors(L):
            zz=pr-g-L.ln()
            return zz.exp()-1,1-(-zz).exp(),sr-M-L.ln(),wr+B-L
        span=I(lpr.ln().l,upr.ln().r)
        y=errors(span)[k]
        assertlt(0,y)
        assertlt(y,Q('.01'))
        def metric(x):
            z=I(p)+I(x);L=z.ln()
            return errors(L)[k]*L**(2 if k==3 else 3)
        assertlt(tt,metric(l));assertlt(metric(r),tt)
        print('local threshold',k,p,l,r,metric(l),metric(r),flush=True)

Finite proof and arithmetic: finite_m.py uses the ordinary
Eratosthenes sieve through 54000000, larger than \(e^{17.8}\).
It accumulates interval sums at integer mesh endpoints \(n\)
with next increment \(\lfloor n/80000\rfloor\) (last endpoint
clipped). Every sum is monotone, so between endpoints it lies
in the interval from the left sum's lower end to the right sum's
upper. Subtract the smooth log term with its entire cell image,
and multiply the error magnitude by the **right** endpoint log
power. This proves the full finite intervals including nonintegers.
For a tighter numerical envelope the exact sums and bracketing
values in this check can be used instead of the constant table.

The sums use signed integer fixed point of scale \(2^{80}\).
For integer \(p=2^k m,\ 1\le m<2\), take \(j=\lfloor4096m\rfloor\)
and evaluate \(\log p=k\log2+\log(j/4096)+\log(1+r)\) with
\(0\le r<1/4096\). Three series terms and the next alternating
remainder bound \(2^{-50}\) suffice. Individual floor/ceil losses
are included. For \(-\log(1-1/p)-1/p\), use the exact outward log
for \(p\le1024\), else orders 2 through 5 with remainder \(<2/p^6\).
The code also checks the smaller local endpoints above, with no
cell-width penalty. For gamma it uses
\(\gamma_{\!E}\in[H_n-\log n-1/(2n),\,H_n-\log n-1/(2n)+1/n^2]\).
Indeed subtract the trapezoidal rule on each interval
\([m,m+1]\) from the integral of \(1/t\) and sum for \(m\ge n\);
the positive trapezoid errors have sum at most
\(\sum_{m\ge n}1/(6m^3)<1/n^2\).
For the tails in \(M,B_3\), use the Dusart \(\theta\) relative
error \(\delta=.2/(\log N)^2\) on \(t\ge N=54000000\)
(Thm. 4.2, row \(k=2,\eta=.2\)). For \(M\)'s square term the
main integral is \(\frac12\int_N^\infty t^{-2}/\log t\,dt\),
bracketed by two adjacent integrated geometric polynomials in
\(1/(1+v/\log N)\) after \(t=N e^v\). Its error is at most
\(\delta(3+1/\log N)/(2N\log N)\); higher powers have total
\(\le1/N^2\) by the integer sum. For \(B_3\) the weight for
\(\theta\) is \(1/[t(t-1)]\); its main integral is
\(w=-\log(1-1/N)\), error at most \(\delta(2/(N-1)+w)\).
These inequalities follow from the tail integration rule in §4.
Thus the normalization is independently enclosed, without
rounding a literature decimal to an allegedly exact constant.

## FKS Lemma 5.2 valid segment, with least real onset

Let \(g(L)=2L^{3/2}e^{-c\sqrt L}\), \(c=.8476836\).
The original Lemma 5.2 (PDF p.17, text 1928–1942) cannot be
invoked on its full printed domain. At 2 and at 2.1, the
actual relative error \(1-\log 2/x\) exceeds \(g(\log x)\)
(directed signs in repair.py). On \([2,3)\) the error has this
exact formula. Its difference subtracted from \(g\) increases
strictly in \(L\): \(g'(L)=\sqrt L e^{-c\sqrt L}(3-c\sqrt L)\)
is at least the product formed from the minimum of each factor
on \([\log2,\log3]\), which exceeds \((\log2)/2\).
Therefore there is a unique root \(r_\psi\) of
\(g(\log x)=1-\log2/x\) in \((2,3)\), with
\(2.29012<r_\psi<2.29014\). The inequality holds on
\([r_\psi,3)\) and fails in a left neighborhood of the root.

On \(3\le x\le e^{40}\) use Dusart Theorem 3.3
(PDF p.8, text 458–475): its .77 bound is below both endpoint
values of \(g\), and \(g\) has just one critical point, a maximum.
On \(40<L\le1000\) use \(1.93378\cdot10^{-8}<g(1000)\),
and on \(1000<L\le2100\) use \(1.94751\cdot10^{-12}<g(2100)\).
These literature-trust step bounds are stated explicitly on the
corresponding strict lower domains in the lemma's original proof;
\(g\) decreases throughout these log intervals. This proves the
repaired enclosed segment, including equality at the left end.

def early_sign():
    L=I('15.4')
    assertlt(10**4,L.exp())
    assertlt(I(10**13).ln(),30)
    assertlt(Q('.047')+Q('8e-12')*(I(30)*3/8).exp()+
             Q('1.838')*(-L/2).exp()+(-5*L/2).exp(),Q('.048'))
    for u,c in [('15.4','.0012'),('18','.0556')]:
        L=I(u)
        cf=1-5*I('3.965')*9/L**2
        assertlt(0,cf)
        low=1-3*I('3.965')*4/L**2-Q('.751')-Q('.048')+cf*(-I(30)/6).exp()/2
        assertlt(Q(c),low)
        print('signed weighted',u,c,low,flush=True)
    assertlt(32321,(I('20.77')/2).exp())
    for u,c in [('20.6','.00015'),('20.77','.0889')]:
        L=I(u)
        delta=I('3.965')*4/L**2 if u=='20.6' else 80/L**3
        main=1-2/L+8/L**2-48/L**3
        assertlt(8,L/2) # keeps the derivative of main positive
        cf=1-I(3)/(2*L)-I('3.965')*9/L**2*(5+3/L)
        assertlt(0,cf)
        low=main-delta*(3+2/L)-Q('.751')-(1+1/L)*Q('.048')-L*(-L/2).exp()+cf*(-I(30)/6).exp()/2
        assertlt(Q(c),low)
        print('signed reciprocal/log',u,c,low,flush=True)

valid from 15.4: after rescaling, put the increasing high
term at 30 and the decaying elementary terms at 15.4.

## 5. Whole-ray comparison

B1 preserves the entire B0 envelope; its new component
intervals are nested wherever used. There is **strict** improvement
throughout \(L\ge168.82\) against the matched B0 constructions
and the listed explicit original-source branches. Here is one
way to prove it without looking for pairwise sampled crossovers.

On that ray the old endpoint intervals contain the symmetric
interval of radius \(f_0(L)=\min(1.046\cdot10^{-12},.0104e^{-L/8})\).
For the CH2 intervals the radius minus center is at least
\(\pi/T-4/T^2\) for \(10^7\le T\le H\), hence \(>1.046\cdot10^{-12}\).
For old density S4 use its final coefficient, and for S5
use \(B_{\rm int}(s)>.0104\) on every row through \(7/8\)
(order-3 lower checks at each right edge). The density-free
bound is larger as well. The much older power-of-log shapes
are larger than \(f_0\): for the \(\theta\) table one may use
the minimum coefficient for each fixed power, and for FKS and
PT the exponential-\(\sqrt L\) shapes have increasing ratio
to \(e^{-L/8}\) on \(L\ge170\). For clarity on the step values:
Dusart Table 1 through \(b<1500\) uses constants \(\ge8.743\cdot10^{-12}\);
from \(b=1500\) its smallest is \(2.358\cdot10^{-20}\).
PT Table 1 starts at 1000 and has all constants \(\ge6.78\cdot10^{-29}\).
FKS Table 5 before 10000 has all constants \(\ge9\cdot10^{-29}\);
the later constants are all at least \(3.95\cdot10^{-359}\).
Compare each group at its left edge against the *decreasing*
\(f_0\). FKS Table 6 instances have \(A>1,R<6\) and exponent
coefficient \(2/\sqrt R<1\); this suffices already at the
first applicable onset. The remaining applicable source shapes
are checked directly by their monotonic ratios. No claim is
made about an uncomputed optimized instantiation of an arbitrary
parameter formula, or about all conceivable B0 theorems.

The old \(I_K\) intervals contain 0 for \(L\ge168.82\), even with
the deterministic center. The old intervals for raw-log and
sum errors contain the symmetric radii \(F(L)/L,F(L)\) as
appropriate, where \(F=\min(1.045\cdot10^{-12},.01e^{-L/8})\).
Indeed their endpoint terms preserve \(f_0\) or \(f_0/L\);
integral terms in §4 contain 0, and any lost radius from signed
prime powers, including the tail over \(p>x\), is bounded
by \(3e^{-L/2}\) in scaled units. This allowance is
less than both \( .001\cdot10^{-12}\) and \( .0004 e^{-L/8}\)
at 168.82 and thereafter. In the \(A/L\) formulas the direct
old weighted CH2 bound contains the same symmetric radius.
Independent original relative and early analytic bounds are
larger than these comparison radii as well (their ratios
against the power floor increase; the short \(\min\) plateau
poses no restriction). Thus converting either old log interval
still leaves relative envelopes at least \(F/L\).

In contrast, use \(d=D_1\) in M4. The code checks \(LV/(1-V)\)
at 168.82 below both \(1.045\cdot10^{-12}\) and \(.01e^{-168.82/8}\).
Its ratios against those two functions decrease thereafter,
by the positive mixture argument (now scale by 0 or by \(1/8\),
both at most \(a_1\)); also \(U\le LV\). This proves strict
improvement in every channel on the entire ray. In particular

## 3. Strict envelope comparisons, now from \(L=168.745\)

The radius floor \(f_0=\min(1.046\cdot10^{-12},.0104e^{-L/8})\)
of mertens.md §5 still works on this slightly enlarged domain.
The source constants and monotonic ratios justify the same
comparisons (on the plateau use through 190 as before);
for the refined B0 mesh its terminal coefficient exceeds
.0104 by the directed check. The two new density-free bounds
each include \(2.091e^{-L/8}\), so do not invalidate the floor.
The S5 and old signed \(K\) alternatives have the same
budget and centers. The new kernel option in §4 below adds
an interval containing 0 for its integral on this ray
(even if the elementary terms are separated as a signed
center: one may bound them by the stated symmetric radius,
and the half-line budget exceeds their magnitude; the
explicit preexisting signed-center variants use only S7/S8).
As before, loss of radius by signed prime powers is at most
\(3e^{-L/2}\) in scaled units. The new checks verify
\(LV/(1-V)< F_*(L)\) for \(L=168.745\), with
\(F_*=\min(1.045\cdot10^{-12},.01e^{-L/8})\) and
\(d=d_{\rm fine,1}\), and both ratios decrease on the ray.
The signed upper \(\pi\)-error before drift subtraction is
also less than both defining quantities of \(F_*\) at the
left endpoint, with the same declining ratios thereafter.
Thus the strict Mertens improvement holds on this enlarged
ray, and so does the strict R4–R5 improvement. No strict
gain on every point before this ray is asserted; B1 retains
all old bounds regardless.

        z=mert_point(L.l,1,d_fine)

            assertlt(z,q);assertlt(p,q)
        for q in (I('1e-15'),Q('.0004')*(-L/8).exp()):
            assertlt(3*(-L/2).exp(),q)
        print('strict floors checked at',L,flush=True)
        L=I(342); v=a(1)*L+L.ln()+I('2.45').ln()

        assertlt((a(1)+1/L)*(1/(v-h)+1/(v+h-2*(2*PI).ln())),I(1)/32)
        for q in (I('1.045e-12'),Q('.01')*(-L/8).exp()):

        print('density-free strict comparison anchors',L,flush=True)

def ram():
    A=Q('450')
    def verify(k,m,a,j,improved=False,fallback=False):
        a,m=Q(a),Q(m)
        d=k+(m==cs[k])
        t=I(A)
        assert d+6 < (A-1)/8
        assertlt(loss(t,t,bD(A,j,fallback),bD(A-1,j,fallback),d)+sum(-c/t**(i-d) for i,c in enumerate(cs) if c<0),
                 cs[d]-(0 if d>k else m))
        if a>=A:return
        cells=0
        def part(l,r):
            nonlocal cells
            p,q=I(l),I(r)
            if improved:
                up,dn=two_errors(l,r,j)
            else:
                up,dn=ub(l,j,r<=58,fallback),ub(F.subtract(l,Q(1)),j,r<=59,fallback)
            lower=resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,up,dn,k)
            if lower.l>m:
                cells+=1;return
            assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,k,j,m,lower)
            mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
            part(l,mid);part(mid,r)
        ends=[a]+[Q(t) for t in [34,35,40,41,58,59,80,125,166,169,189,190,230,300,375] if a<t<A]+[A]
        for l,r in zip(ends,ends[1:]): part(l,r)
        return cells
    for k,m,a,b in ROWS:
        t0=verify(k,m,a,0);t1=verify(k,m,b,1)
        print('onset',k,m,a,b,t0,t1,flush=True)
    for k,a,m0,m1 in FIXED:
        print('fixed',k,a,m0,m1,verify(k,m0,a,0),verify(k,m1,a,1),flush=True)

def den_limit(L,j):
    # For all U>=L, exp(a*U) times the two scaled bounds of mux
    # are nonincreasing (L>=170). For products apply expm1 <= z/(1-z).
    L=I(L)
    a=I(1)/8 if j==0 else I(5)/32
    d=ds(L.l)[j]
    v,w=mux(L,j,d,'1.34')
    assert 0 <= w.l <= w.r < 1
    return v*(a*L).exp(), L*w*(a*L).exp(),L*w*(a*L).exp()/(1-w)
    for a in [170,175,180,185,190,200,225,250,300,400,500,600,800,1000,1500,2500,5000,10000]:
        print('power limits',a,[tuple(str(x.r) for x in den_limit(a,j)) for j in (0,1)],flush=True)

source_references.full_readback:
## Replay

From this directory with the offline interpreter:
    
    /usr/bin/python3.10 -B bounds.py all
    /usr/bin/python3.10 -B finite_m.py
    /usr/bin/python3.10 -B repair.py
    /usr/bin/python3.10 -B advance.py certify

The first two outputs match the old replay.txt and finite_replay.txt;
their fresh transcripts are repair_original_replay.txt and
repair_finite_replay.txt. New evidence is in repair_replay.txt and
advance_replay.txt. The optional advance.py explore mode is **not**
a whole-ray proof. Directed Decimal arithmetic uses 48 significant
digits; arithmetic operations are outward and exp/ln enclose their
correctly rounded implementations by adjacent Decimal numbers.
Pi uses Machin's identity; finite counts and sieve use exact integer
operations. The written proofs supply the domain and monotonicity
arguments for numerical tests. No Lean or source-first PV is claimed.

S=1<<80
# The last cell ends beyond exp(17.8) (join to bounds.py).
LIMIT=54000000
START=500000
DEN=80000
def floor(x): return int(x.to_integral_value(rounding='ROUND_FLOOR'))
def ceil(x): return int(x.to_integral_value(rounding='ROUND_CEILING'))
def snap(x):
    x=S*x
    return floor(x.l),ceil(x.r)
def fixed(l,r):return I(l,r)/S
def gamma():
    n=200000
    w=sum(S//i for i in range(1,n+1))
    g=fixed(w,w+n)-I(n).ln()-I(1)/(2*n)
    return I(g.l,(g+I(1)/(n*n)).r)

def sieve(n):
    b=bytearray(b'\x01')*(n+1); b[:2]=b'\x00\x00'
    for p in range(2,isqrt(n)+1):
        if b[p]:
            b[p*p::p]=b'\x00'*((n-p*p)//p+1)
    p=2
    while p!=-1:
        yield p
        p=b.find(b'\x01',p+1)

def run():
    assertlt(I('17.8').exp(),LIMIT)
    log2lo,log2hi=snap(LN2)
    logs=[snap((I(j)/4096).ln()) for j in range(4096,8192)]
    g=gamma()
    gs=snap(g)
    Mlo,Mhi=0,0
    Blo,Bhi=0,0
    plo=phi=slo=shi=tlo=thi=0
    L=[]
    critical={}
    after={912559:912560,2278379:2278383}
    n=START
    checkpoints=[]
    while n<LIMIT:
        checkpoints.append(n);n+=n//DEN
    checkpoints.append(LIMIT)
    t=iter(checkpoints)
    n=next(t)
    for p in sieve(LIMIT):
        while p>n:
            L.append((n,plo,phi,slo,shi,tlo,thi));n=next(t)
        # k*log(2)+log(j/4096)+log(1+r)
        k=p.bit_length()-1; j=(4096*p)>>k; d=j<<k; z=4096*p-d
        lower,upper=logs[j-4096]
        v=S*z//d; z2=z*z; d2=d*d
        w=S*z2//(2*d2); u=S*z2*z//(3*d2*d)
        # Alternating series, first omitted term <= 2^-50.
        lp=k*log2lo+lower+v-w+u-1-(S>>50)
        hp=k*log2hi+upper+v-w+u+2
        quot=S//p
        slo+=quot;shi+=quot+1
        tlo+=lp//p;thi+=hp//p+1
        if p<=1024:
            al,au=snap(-(1-I(1)/p).ln()-I(1)/p)
        else:
            p2=p*p;p3=p2*p;p4=p3*p;p5=p4*p;p6=p5*p
            al=S//(2*p2)+S//(3*p3)+S//(4*p4)+S//(5*p5)
            au=al+5+2*S//p6
        Mlo+=al;Mhi+=au
        plo+=quot+al;phi+=quot+au+1
        Blo+=lp//(p*(p-1));Bhi+=hp//(p*(p-1))+1
        if p in after:
            critical[p]=(fixed(plo,phi),fixed(slo,shi),fixed(tlo,thi))
        assert all(not a<p<=b for a,b in after.items())
    L.append((LIMIT,plo,phi,slo,shi,tlo,thi))
    assert len(L)==len(checkpoints)
    l=I(LIMIT).ln()
    delta=Q('.2')/l**2
    k=I(1)/(2*LIMIT)/l
    v=I(1);poly=I(1);even=None
    for n in range(1,10):
        v=-v*n/l;poly+=v
        if n==8:even=poly
    rad=k*delta*(3+1/l)
    mtail=I((k*poly-rad).l,(k*even+rad+I(1)/(LIMIT**2)).r)
    w=-(1-I(1)/LIMIT).ln()
    rad=delta*(2/I(LIMIT-1)+w)
    btail=w+I(rad.r.copy_negate(),rad.r)
    M=g-fixed(Mlo,Mhi)-mtail
    B=g+fixed(Blo,Bhi)+btail
    print('finite constants',M,B,g,flush=True)

def ram_row(k,m,u,j,f,signed):
    m,u=Q(m),Q(u); d=k+(m==cs[k]); T=Q(450 if k<=8 else 650); t=I(T)
    assert d+6 < (T-1)/8 and d+4 < 21
    assertlt(loss(t,t,primeB(T,j,f),primeB(T-1,j,f),d)+sum(-c/t**(i-d) for i,c in enumerate(cs) if c<0),
             cs[d]-(0 if d>k else m))
    def part(l,r):
        p,q=I(l),I(r)
        ub,wb=errors(l,r,j,f,signed)
        if (resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,ub,wb,k)).l>m:return 1
        assert r-l>Q('.000001'),(l,r,k,j,m,resmain(p,q,k)-loss(p,q,ub,wb,k))
        mid=N.divide(N.add(l,r),Q(2))
        return part(l,mid)+part(mid,r)
    ends=[u]+[Q(t) for t in [34,35,40,41,58,59,80,125,166,169,189,190,230,300,375] if u<t<T]+[T]
    return sum(part(l,r) for l,r in zip(ends,ends[1:]))
def split_m_ray(j):
    L=I(300); aa=a(j)
    v=aa*L+L.ln()+I('2.45').ln()
    log2pi=(2*PI).ln()
    assertlt(0,v-h)
    assertlt(0,v+h-2*log2pi)
    assertlt((aa+1/L)*(1/(v-h)+1/(v+h-2*log2pi)),aa)
    assertlt(1,L.ln()+I('2.45').ln()-log2pi)
    c=1/(2*PI)+(Q('.137')*h+Q('.443'))/(H*h*(h-log2pi))
    neg=c*(h-log2pi)**2
    target=Q('.00408' if j else '.00262')
    for l in range(300,2501,5):
        L=I(l); r=l+5
        _,w=mux(L,j,d_split(l,j),'1.34')
        assert 0<=w.l<=w.r<1
        # The last check drops the entire negative term for the analytic tail.
        ans=(L*w*(aa*L).exp()/L**2+neg/L**2-(0 if l==2500 else neg/I(r)**2))/(1-w)
        assertlt(ans,target)
    print('split M whole-ray',j,300,target,440,ans,flush=True)

def sqrt(x): return (I(x).ln()/2).exp()
def shape(L):
    z=sqrt(L)
    return 2*L*z*(-I('.8476836')*z).exp()
def fks():
    L0,L1=LN2,I(3).ln()
    assertlt(shape(L0),1-LN2/2)
    assertlt(shape(I('2.1').ln()),1-LN2/I('2.1'))
    c=I('.8476836')
    assertlt(LN2/2,sqrt(L0)*(-c*sqrt(L1)).exp()*(3-c*sqrt(L1)))
    for z,sgn in [('2.29012',-1),('2.29014',1)]:
        x=I(z); v=shape(x.ln())-(1-LN2/x)
        print('FKS onset bracket',z,v)
        assertlt(0,sgn*v)
    for u in (L1,I(40)): assertlt(Q('.77'),shape(u))
    assertlt(3,c*sqrt(40))
    assertlt(Q('1.93378e-8'),shape(I(1000)))
    assertlt(Q('1.94751e-12'),shape(I(2100)))
    assertlt(Q('.77'),Q('9.22022')/2*shape(L0))

def pt():
    x=I('2.9')
    assertlt(1-LN2/2,1-LN2/x)
    delta=1-LN2/3
    t=LN2; p=2; ps=[2]
    for n in range(3,600):
        if any(n%r==0 for r in ps if r*r<=n): continue
        if n!=3: assertlt(1-t/n,delta)
        assertlt(t/p-1,delta)
        ps.append(n);p=n;t=t+I(n).ln()
    assertlt(1-t/599,delta)
    assertlt(t/p-1,delta)
    L=I(3914)
    bd=bD(L,0,True)
    assertlt(L**6*bd,720)
    assertlt(sum(I(factorial(k))/L**(k-5) for k in range(6,21))+L**5*(bd+err(L)),Q('.19'))
    B=1/L+196/L**2
    assertlt(Q('.19'),720*B)
    R=I('5.573412'); c=I('1.89')
    def last(U):
        return U**5*I('379.7')*(I('1.52')*(U/R).ln()-c*sqrt(U/R)).exp()
    assertlt(Q('.99'),1-Q('.48')/3800-c/(2*sqrt(R*3800)))
    assertlt(16*(-I(2)).exp()/(8*PI),500)
    assertlt(I(1169)/Q('6.455'),500)
    v=I('3.04')/c
    assertlt(462*(Q('3.04')*v.ln()-c*v).exp(),500)
    assertlt(500/LN2**2,1100)
    assertlt(1100*L**6*(-I(114)).exp()+last(L)/(Q('.99')*L),last(L)*B)
    print('PT small-piece and domination checks OK; a(anchor)',last(L))

if __name__=='__main__':
    fks();pt()
    L=I(100); logder=cH*(-L/2).exp()/(2*A_C(L))
    assertlt(I('1e-8'),logder)
    assertlt(logder,I('1e-7'))
    print('CH2 log slope at 100',logder)
